scope.summary: This standard specifies the dimensions, tolerances, materials, and mechanical requirements for hot-dip galvanized hexagon head transmission tower bolts in the size range M12 to M24 [2]. These bolts are intended for use in the construction of electrical transmission towers, electrical sub-stations, and similar steel structures [2]. It explicitly states that these bolts are not suitable for applications requiring improved low-temperature material characteristics [2].

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Industrial Fasteners / Transmission Line Hardware) [1, 2]
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the statutory 'Bolts, Nuts and Fasteners (Quality Control) Order' issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all hexagon head transmission tower bolts must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to certify chemical, physical, and mechanical compliance. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified structural fasteners in India is a statutory offense. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial steel fasteners.

requirements.detail: Every package of transmission tower bolts must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) to certify compliance [5].
All dimensions specified in Fig. 1 and Table 1 are required to be verified on the bolt prior to the execution of the hot-dip galvanizing process [4].
Prior to hot-dip galvanizing, the bolt threads must be tested and conform with Go and Not Go threaded ring gauges in accordance with IS 2334 [4].

The standard specifies nominal thread sizes range from M12 to M24 [2]. Grip ranges (representing the total thickness of the connected material, excluding washers) and length combinations must strictly conform to Table 2 [4, 8]. Size M22 is designated as non-preferred [8].

To prevent wet storage strain (white rust), galvanized bolts, nuts, and washers must be passivated immediately after galvanizing by dipping in a 0.15 percent solution of sodium dichromate with 0.5 percent concentrated sulphuric acid maintained above 32°C [11].

During load testing, the mechanical shear loading rate must be controlled between 7 to 13 mm per minute [11]. The maximum shear stress coincident with bolt failure represents the shear strength and must comply with standard property thresholds [11].

Bolts are designated by nomenclature, thread size, nominal length, standard number, and property class [6]. Suffix N indicates supply with nut, and W indicates supply with plain washer [6]. Examples include: 'Transmission Tower Bolt M16 x 50 N — 5.6 IS 12427' [6] or 'Transmission Tower Bolt M16 x 50 NW — 5.6 IS 12427' [7].
Each bolt head must carry the property class marking (conforming to IS 1367 Part 3) along with the manufacturer's identification symbol permanently marked on the head [7].

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 12427 : 2001 is the mandatory national Indian Standard safety specification regulating hot-dip galvanized hexagon head bolts (and their matching nuts and washers) designed specifically for constructing power transmission towers, electrical sub-stations, and similar heavy steel frames [2]. Under India's statutory Fasteners Quality Control Order (QCO), all such transmission tower bolts supplied domestically must be certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards and carry the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) [5]. It covers sizes M12 to M24 (with M22 designated as non-preferred), specifying precise grip ranges to ensure structural stability in connected joints [2, 8]. To survive severe outdoor weather, it mandates hot-dip zinc coatings and an immediate sodium dichromate passivation bath to prevent white rust formation during transport or storage [5, 11].
